title: Deterministic nonbipartite Ramanujan graphs in every fixed degree
main_claim: For every fixed d>=3 there is a deterministic algorithm that runs in time polynomial in n (exponent depending on d). For every sufficiently large even n it outputs a simple d-regular graph whose nonconstant adjacency eigenvalues all lie strictly inside (-2sqrt(d-1), 2sqrt(d-1)), so the graph is Ramanujan, connected and nonbipartite. The construction runs a discounted-account (pessimistic estimator) pairing of stubs down to a separated boundary, completes the pairing against a smooth Woodbury-continued path reference, and finally makes M ~ n^{1/3+10a} biased simultaneous edge switches. Those switches are derandomized with pairwise-independent seeds, and every candidate is checked by an exact rational inertia test.

issues.location: repair.tex, Lemma repair-bulk (typical edge blocks), item 2 input
issues.description: The typical-edge argument assumes a bounded number of actual nonbacktracking paths between fixed endpoints for every length k < L, where L is about (2/3)log_q n. That assumption is supplied by the structural core accounts (eq. 3) through the bounded-excess argument in the foundations section. I checked that this argument goes through, since (r_*+1)L <= r_*J with J = 0.9 log_q n. However, the bound is only as strong as the deterministic maintenance of the core accounts through cleanup, and I only skimmed that part. This is not a gap, only the least directly verified link in the chain.
issues.evidence: "The number of actual nonbacktracking paths of any length k<L between fixed endpoints is bounded by a constant."

Checked by hand: the ideal switch block (det -1, inverse K_sigma); the switch sign sI - sigma A' = sI - sigma A + U C U^T; the Schur/Woodbury inertia argument and the near Schur complement; the uniform mean -4x_i/((d-2)n); the tilt bias 4Tr(K M K M)/(B_* J_T n), including the cross-term bookkeeping; the positivity of the tilted density; every exponent ratio in the repair margin table; the generating function W = sum (sigma h)^j Q_j with M = z - sigma A_e - h D; -dM/dh; the Woodbury condition and coefficient -sigma h P_t on both P_t eigenspaces with normalization m_h; the finite-population pair-average formula (2) and the pure-swap single-A identity; the trace identity for Delta Y; the pencil root-location lemma (including the double-root and y<=0 cases) and the Cauchy bound; m'/m^2 = 1 + h^{-2} behind (10)-(11); the derivation of the energy gap (46) from (11); the logistic drift -(2/l)u(1-u) against the comparator u_bar and the omega_l scaling; and the Phase B/final-matching exponent requirements (chi < r_P, l_3 B_B = o(1), B_B = o(sqrt e) iff g + r < 0.35a). Not read in detail: the cleanup section (946 lines) and the early-phase trace, low-square and index-word lemmas (roughly lines 120-890 of early.tex).
